items.headline: Croatian Crime Drama ‘Red Water,’ Directed by Cannes Prizewinner Antoneta Alamat Kusijanovic, to Be Co-Produced by ZDF/Arte, Beta Film (EXCLUSIVE)
items.facts: Beta Film teamed up with ZDF/Arte and Antitalent to co‑produce the Croatian drama “Red Water.”

framing.publicBrief: At a bright early‑morning meeting in a repurposed factory loft, Beta Film, ZDF/Arte and Antitalent sit around a table. The three companies have just signed an exclusive agreement to co‑produce the Croatian crime drama ‘Red Water,’ directed by Cannes prizewinner Antoneta Alamat Kusijanovic. Each party will contribute funding, distribution channels and talent, and each hopes the series will boost its profile and revenue in European markets. The deal hinges on everyone honoring their commitments as the production moves into shooting.

roleFlavor.contributor: You are the coalition of Beta Film, ZDF/Arte and Antitalent, each holding a share of the financing and distribution plan and watching the others' contributions closely.

howItWorks: All three firms must deliver their pledged resources on schedule.
If any firm falls short, the others may have to cover the gap or delay the series.
Successful joint delivery unlocks shared broadcast slots across Europe.
A failure by one party reduces the series' reach and damages reputations.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Decide how your coalition proceeds with the co‑production commitments

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: All three companies meet their obligations, the series launches on multiple networks and raises each partner’s profile.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One partner withdraws funding, forcing the others to scramble, delaying the series and harming all reputations.
outcomes.MIXED: Some contributions arrive late, the launch is postponed but the series eventually airs with reduced exposure.

framing.publicBrief: The sun rises over the Adriatic coast as the final terms for the Croatian crime drama ‘Red Water’ are settled. Directed by Cannes prizewinner Antoneta Alamat Kusijanovic, the project requires a unified front. Beta Film, ZDF/Arte, and Antitalent must align their resources. The script is locked, the cast is waiting, and the distribution rights hang in the balance. One party holds the leverage to greenlight the shoot; the other must decide whether to accept the terms or walk away from the set entirely.

roleFlavor.proposer: You hold the distribution leverage. You set the terms for the co-production. If the other side refuses, the project stalls, and your investment sits idle.
roleFlavor.responder: You hold the creative assets and local access. You must decide if the deal offered by the financiers is worth your talent and time, or if you should walk away.

howItWorks: Beta Film and ZDF/Arte set the production terms.
Antitalent holds the final say to accept or reject.
Acceptance leads to immediate filming and shared revenue.
Rejection cancels the deal, leaving all parties with nothing.

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Red Water enters production with full funding and distribution.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: The deal collapses; the project is shelved indefinitely.
outcomes.MIXED: Negotiations stall as parties seek better terms.

items.headline: Can festivals leave the land better than they found it?
items.facts: Festival organisers offered live recycling workshops while attendees brought plastic waste to be processed.

framing.narrativeTitle: Festival Organisers and Attendees: A Plastic Swap
framing.publicBrief: Festival organisers set up live recycling workshops on the grounds, inviting festival attendees to bring their plastic waste for processing. The organisers aim to clean the site and showcase sustainability, while attendees hope to learn and dispose of trash responsibly. The event promises a cleaner festival area for everyone.

roleFlavor.contributor: You are the festival organiser, holding the schedule, the workshop kits, and the promise of a greener venue. You can see the line of attendees with plastic bags, but you cannot see which ones will act

howItWorks: Festival organisers control the workshops and the processing line.
Festival attendees bring plastic waste and decide whether to hand it over.
If both sides engage, the waste is processed and the grounds are cleaned.
If either side does not participate, the waste remains and the site stays dirty.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Decide how to engage with the recycling effort

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Both organisers and attendees hand over plastic, the waste is processed, and the grounds are cleaner.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One side refuses to participate, leaving plastic on the grounds.
outcomes.MIXED: Partial participation leaves some waste processed and some left behind.

items.headline: 270,000 Square Miles Around Easter Island to Become Indigenous-Managed Ocean Reserve
items.facts: Indigenous people of Easter Island will hold majority voting power on a sea council governing a large marine reserve, sharing seats with Chilean officials.

items.headline: Sundance Breakout ‘Thelma’ Set for Mandarin Remake by Stars Collective, Titled ‘Grandma, Please’ (EX
items.facts: Stars Collective acquired the Mandarin-language remake rights to the Sundance film “Thelma.”

framing.publicBrief: Stars Collective announces it has secured the Mandarin-language remake rights to the Sundance breakout ‘Thelma.’ The rights holders have agreed to transfer the property, opening a path for a new version titled ‘Grandma, Please.’ Both parties stand to benefit: Stars Collective can tap the Chinese market, while the original owners receive a licensing fee and broader exposure for the story.

roleFlavor.proposer: Stars Collective holds the financing and production plan for the Mandarin version, ready to launch a major release in China.
roleFlavor.responder: The rights holders control the original intellectual property and must decide whether the offered terms reflect the film’s value.

items.headline: AI automation startup Relay shuts down, staff joins Google’s Chrome team
items.facts: Relay announced it is shutting down and some staff, including its CEO, are joining Google’s Chrome team.

framing.narrativeTitle: Relay Shuts Down, Staff Joins Google
framing.publicBrief: Relay has announced its immediate shutdown. At the same time, a group of its staff, including its CEO, are joining Google’s Chrome team. The decision marks the end of one venture and the beginning of another within the tech ecosystem. The move consolidates talent and resources under Google’s umbrella, ending the independent operations of Relay.

framing.publicBrief: Relay has announced it is shutting down. Its staff, including the CEO, are joining Google’s Chrome team. The independent venture ends as talent consolidates under Google.

roleFlavor.guesser: You are a Relay employee deciding how to frame the move to Google.

items.headline: Wetherspoons pubs ban playing music or taking calls on phone speakers
items.facts: Wetherspoons announced a ban on customers playing music or taking calls on speaker, asking them to use earphones or silent mode.

items.headline: Tupac Shakur murder trial: gang leader plotted killing to avenge beating of nephew, court hears
items.facts: Duane “Keffe D” Davis is on trial for allegedly orchestrating the 1996 drive‑by shooting that killed Tupac Shakur in retaliation for an attack on his nephew.

items.headline: Anthropic’s annualized revenue surges to $65B
items.facts: Anthropic reported annualized revenue of $65 billion, up from $47 billion in May, and investors expect continued growth.

items.headline: Water companies in England and Wales explore ‘surge pricing’ during drought
items.facts: Water companies in England and Wales could be allowed to raise bills during drought periods under Ofwat proposals linking charges to water scarcity.
